answer:
I found two commits since v2.0.0 that broke the tests. Each needed a one-line fix in the source. The full suite now passes (517 of 517), and no tests were changed.

1. **`958d3ae` (thousands separators in `formatMoney`)**: the cents were padded on the wrong side. `padEnd(2, "0")` turned 1 cent into `"10"`, so `$0.01` printed as `$0.10`. I changed it back to `padStart` in `src/money.js`. The comma grouping that commit added still works.

2. **`4188e9a` (per-line discount groundwork)**: it changed the taxed amount to `subtotal` alone. That meant order-level codes like SPRING10 were no longer taken off before tax, which broke the CA-ON totals. I changed `src/invoice.js` so tax is charged on `subtotal - discount` again. Line discounts are still taken off before tax, because they're already part of the subtotal. The rest of that commit is unchanged: the `lineDiscounts` and `taxable` fields, the empty-invoice check, and the line discounts row in the rendered invoice.

The other three commits (currencies, US state taxes, JSDoc) were fine. The changes are not committed.

tool_calls.input: git log --oneline v2.0.0..HEAD && cat package.json && ls -R | grep -v node_modules | head -40 && npm
npm test 2>&1 | grep -E "FAIL|✕"; git show 958d3ae -- src; git show 4188e9a --stat
sed -i 's/padEnd(2, "0")/padStart(2, "0")/' src/money.js && git show 4188e9a -- src && cat src/invoi
sed -i 's/const taxable = subtotal;/const taxable = subtotal - discount;/' src/invoice.js && npm tes
